original_test_intent: Enable and persist platform GPU SR-IOV, provision the approved virtual function to an approved guest, and prove the VM boots and sees the correct detailed GPU VF identity/capabilities without damaging host GPU service.
original_method: Confirm platform/GPU/firmware SR-IOV support; define PF/VF UUID/BDF/count and IOMMU/hypervisor/guest plan; preserve host baseline and OOB rollback; operator changes BIOS and reboots; verify setting/IOMMU/VFs persist; create isolated guest with exact VF; install approved guest driver; collect host assignment and full guest lspci -vvv/driver/health; stop/handoff VM and restore only by operator plan.
manual_activity: Operator enables/saves BIOS SR-IOV, controls reboot and supplies/installs approved VM/VF configuration; agent may verify host/guest evidence after these steps.
required_inputs: Platform/GPU/BIOS/firmware SR-IOV support and expected enabled state
PF UUID/BDF, requested VF count and PF-to-VF mapping
IOMMU and host GPU/VF driver/provisioning method
Approved QEMU/libvirt/hypervisor config and isolated VM image/credentials
Guest GPU VF driver and expected lspci/capability fields
Maintenance/job drain, console/OOB and BIOS/VF rollback plan
safety_requirements: Never improvise BIOS settings or VF count
Do not assign a production PF/VF or wrong BDF to guest
Require operator/OOB control before BIOS save/reboot
Preserve host/guest logs and ownership mapping
Stop guest/remove assignment on errors; no GPU reset or automatic retry
agent_execution_scope: After operator actions verify BIOS/IOMMU/VF persistence
Collect full host and guest PCI/driver/capability evidence
Coordinate safe guest stop/handoff and report without verdict
engineer_actions: Approve platform support, VF/guest plan and expected fields

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: A host grep cannot prove guest-visible GPU VF identity or detailed lspci capabilities; credentialed SSH is unsafe.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After operator BIOS/reboot and approved VF assignment, collect exact host PF/VF/IOMMU/hypervisor mapping and complete guest `lspci -vvv` plus guest driver/health for the assigned VF.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: BIOS SR-IOV, reboot, VM install/boot and guest lspci -vvv plus 60-minute estimates are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use an identity chain from host PF through VF BDF/hypervisor assignment to guest PCI device and capability fields, with before/after host ownership and recovery evidence.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Proves the requested guest path rather than a host-only device list.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: VF enumeration on the host does not establish VM installation, assignment or guest functionality.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Incorrect BIOS/IOMMU or passthrough can strand devices or prevent boot; physical console/OOB and rollback are mandatory.

project_override_considerations: Virtualization owner defines supported VF count, PF/VF lifecycle, guest driver and canonical guest-visible capability/identity oracle.
expected_evidence: Operator BIOS save/reboot and persisted SR-IOV/IOMMU state
Host PF/VF UUID/BDF/count/driver and provisioning records
Hypervisor/VM image/config plus exact VF assignment
Guest OS/driver and complete lspci -vvv/capability/health output
VM shutdown/handoff, final host GPU health, rollback/disposition and verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Master consistently defines BIOS SR-IOV, VM installation and guest lspci verification; missing VF/hypervisor/field specifics are required project inputs.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Platform support and VM inputs require confirmation but are provisionable; static review is complete.

review_improvement: Builds a complete PF-to-VF-to-guest identity chain and preserves mandatory operator control for BIOS, reboot and VM lifecycle.
independent_technical_reasoning: SR-IOV enablement alone does not create or assign a GPU VF. Correctness spans firmware persistence, IOMMU grouping, host PF/VF ownership, hypervisor attachment and guest driver/capabilities. A host grep can show the device while the guest sees nothing or the wrong function, so full guest lspci and identity mapping are essential, alongside rollback for PCI assignment failures.
